blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around North Shore Pt Moody

items.t: "North Shore" is the board (GVR) sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report (listed there as "North Shore"); it is not an official City of Port Moody OCP neighbourhood name. The official OCP areas along the north side of the Port Moody Arm of Burrard Inlet are Ioco, Pleasantside and April Road, and the Heritage Mountain grouping (Heritage Mountain, Twin Creeks, Noons Creek, Mountain Meadows, Heritage Woods). The north shore runs along the north side of the inlet from the Burnaby border and Ioco in the west to Anmore and Belcarra in the north and east.
Nearby areas: Port Moody Centre across the inlet, Heritage Woods PM on the hills above, Anmore and Belcarra to the north, Burnaby to the west.

Roads: Ioco Road is the primary traffic corridor for the north shore neighbourhoods, connecting south to St. Johns Street, Barnet Highway and the Moody Centre and Inlet Centre stations — the only through-corridor, so showings, school runs and the commute all run on one road. TransLink buses run along Ioco Road to Moody Centre Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express).
Port Moody community — Detached median $1,685,000, $608/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 33 days; Condos & Townhomes median $715,000, $666/sq ft, 94% sale-to-list, 29 days.

Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based. SD43 schools on the north shore include Pleasantside, Aspenwood, Heritage Mountain and Mountain Meadows elementary schools, Eagle Mountain Middle (in Anmore) and Heritage Woods Secondary.

Parks, recreation and health: Old Orchard Park is on the north shore and is a starting point for the Shoreline Trail, with Port Moody's only swimming beach (salt-water); Rocky Point Park at the head of the inlet has a pier, boat launch, outdoor pool and skate park. Old Orchard Hall is at 646 Bentley Road; the Port Moody Recreation Complex is at 300 Ioco Road; Port Moody Public Library is at 100 Newport Drive. Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, south of the inlet, is the in-city hospital.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in North Shore Pt Moody

items.t: OCP — Port Moody Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2026, No. 3522 (adopted April 28, 2026; repeals Bylaw No. 2955 — never cite 2955 as current): Chapter 14 covers the north shore in Section 14.2 (Pleasantside and April Road), Section 14.3 (the Heritage Mountain grouping) and Section 14.4 (Ioco Lands, the former Imperial Oil lands).
Zoning — Port Moody Zoning Bylaw, 2018, No. 2937: Secondary suites are allowed in all single-detached zones except manufactured-home parks, and a secondary suite may not be stratified.

Small-lot subdivision — the one real subdivision route on this shore: subdivision from RS1 to RS1-S (minimum 9 m width and 325 m² lot area) is available only in Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside where the OCP designates Single Family–Low Density — Pleasantside is the one north shore area on that list. Confirm the specific lot's designation with the City before pricing a split.

The documented process instead: subdivision runs against the zone minimums and the RS1-S standard above, and servicing is confirmed with the City for the parcel (utilities billed separately; 2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026).

Heritage — Ioco townsite: the Ioco townsite is a heritage conservation area; a heritage alteration permit can be required for changes, including exterior work on a townsite lot — check heritage status before planning any work there.

ALR rules (for completeness — no north shore ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

Property transfer tax — worked example (inputs + tier math): on a $1,000,000 lot-and-house purchase, fully residential, no exemption — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% on $200,000–$1,000,000 ($16,000) = $18,000. Anchors: $500K→$8,000; $700K→$12,000; $800K cap→$14,000 ($6,000 fully qualifying FTHB); $900K→$16,000; $1.5M→$28,000; $2.0M→$38,000; $3.5M→$93,000 INCLUDING the further 2% tier over $3M (tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000).

blocks.text: Good to know about North Shore Pt Moody

items.t: Pleasantside holds a subdivision tool most of the city does not. It is one of only three areas (with Moody Centre and Seaview, both south of the inlet) where RS1-S small-lot subdivision is available, and only where the OCP designates Single Family–Low Density — a lot-by-lot designation check, not a shore-wide right.

Local rules that affect duplexes in North Shore Pt Moody

Secondary suites are allowed in all single-detached zones except manufactured-home parks, and a secondary suite may not be stratified.

Small-lot subdivision: Subdivision from RS1 to RS1-S (minimum 9 m width and 325 m² lot area) is available only in Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside where the OCP designates Single Family–Low Density — Pleasantside is the one north shore area on that list.

Heritage — Ioco townsite: The Ioco townsite is a heritage conservation area, where a heritage alteration permit can be required for changes; a duplex conversion or exterior work on a townsite property needs that check first.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot on Port Moody's north shore?
faq.a: No verified offering exists — the shore is built out, and land here trades as a house on its fee-simple lot in Pleasantside / April Road or the Heritage Mountain subdivisions.

faq.q: Is "North Shore" an official Port Moody neighbourhood?
faq.a: No — it is the board (MLS) sub-area name. The OCP areas on the north shore are Ioco, Pleasantside and April Road, and the Heritage Mountain grouping, so heritage, small-lot and development rules have to be looked up under those names, under OCP Bylaw 2026, No. 3522.

faq.q: Can a Pleasantside lot be split into small lots?
faq.a: Pleasantside is one of only three areas where the RS1-S small-lot standard is available (minimum 9 m width, 325 m² lot area, and only where the OCP designates Single Family–Low Density) — the other two are Moody Centre and Seaview, both south of the inlet. Confirm the specific lot with the City; SSMUH in RS/RT zones outside transit-oriented areas is the broader route.

faq.q: Are there any townhouses — or townhouse lots — on the north shore?
faq.a: Platform's townhouse-form units are Port Moody Centre ground, counted nowhere as townhomes.

faq.q: What is happening with the Ioco lands?
faq.a: Future planning only: OCP Section 14.4 addresses future planning for the former Imperial Oil lands, and no specific active presale project on the north shore was verified on a developer or City page.

faq.q: Is there a duplex complex on Port Moody's north shore I can buy into?
faq.a: No — none is verified by name. The duplex form here is individual two-unit homes on RS/RT lots under the SSMUH permission; the area's OCP mix is single-detached homes, townhouses and a small number of apartments.

faq.q: Can I split a Pleasantside lot into small lots?
faq.a: Pleasantside is one of only three areas with the RS1-S small-lot standard (minimum 9 m width, 325 m², OCP Single Family–Low Density areas only) — confirm the specific lot's designation with the City.

faq.q: Can a duplex here carry a secondary suite?
faq.a: Port Moody allows secondary suites in all single-detached zones except manufactured-home parks, and a suite may not be stratified; read the current zoning text for the lot before counting rental income.
No — it is the board sub-area name; the OCP areas are Ioco, Pleasantside and April Road, plus the Heritage Mountain grouping.
